full_name: Two-Phase Randomized Stochastic Gradient Free Method (2-RSGF) for Unconstrained Nonconvex Stochastic Zeroth-Order Optimization
source_reference: Lan, First-Order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020 (Theorem 6.4)

problem.description: Unconstrained nonconvex stochastic optimization problem represented by an expectation and accessed through a stochastic zeroth-order oracle.

formalization_prerequisites: For each fixed s, provide an increasing filtration \(\mathcal{F}_{s,0}\subseteq\mathcal{F}_{s,1}\subseteq\cdots\) and make \(\bar{x}_s\) measurable with respect to \(\mathcal{F}_{s,0}\).
For each k, make \(\Delta_{s,k}\) measurable with respect to \(\mathcal{F}_{s,k}\), square-integrable, and conditionally centered: \(\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{s,k}\mid\mathcal{F}_{s,k-1}]=0\).
Supply the per-increment second-moment bound \(\mathbb{E}[\|\Delta_{s,k}\|^2]\le\mathscr{D}_N\), where the source defines \(\mathscr{D}_N\) in (6.1.88).

main_theorem.statement_math: \text{Under Assumptions 13 and 15, the following statements hold for the 2-RSGF method applied to problem (6.1.47). (a) Let }\bar{\mathscr{B}}_N\text{ be defined in (6.1.72). We have }\operatorname{Prob}\left\{\|\nabla f(\bar{x}^*)\|^2 \ge 8L\bar{\mathscr{B}}_N + \frac{3(n+4)L^2D_f^2}{2N} + \frac{24(n+4)\lambda}{T}\left[L\bar{\mathscr{B}}_N + \frac{(n+4)L^2D_f^2}{N} + \sigma^2\right]\right\} \le \frac{S+1}{\lambda}+2^{-S},\quad \forall\lambda>0;\text{ (b) Let }\varepsilon>0\text{ and }\Lambda\in(0,1)\text{ be given. If }S=S(\Lambda)\text{ as in (6.1.32), }N=\hat{N}(\varepsilon):=\max\left\{\frac{12(n+4)(6LD_f)^2}{\varepsilon},\left[72L\sqrt{n+4}\left(\widetilde{D}+\frac{D_f^2}{\widetilde{D}}\right)\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon}\right]^2\right\},\ T=\hat{T}(\varepsilon,\Lambda):=\frac{24(n+4)(S+1)}{\Lambda}\max\left\{1,\frac{6\sigma^2}{\varepsilon}\right\},\text{ then the 2-RSGF method can compute an }(\varepsilon,\Lambda)\text{-solution of problem (6.1.47) after taking at most }2S(\Lambda)[\hat{N}(\varepsilon)+\hat{T}(\varepsilon,\Lambda)]\text{ calls to the SZO.}
main_theorem.measure: high-probability stationarity guarantee and SZO oracle complexity

key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Suppose that the stepsizes }\{\gamma_k\}\text{ are set to }\gamma_k=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n+4}}\min\left\{\frac{1}{4L\sqrt{n+4}},\frac{\widetilde{D}}{\sigma\sqrt{N}}\right\},\ k=1,\ldots,N,\text{ for some }\widetilde{D}>0.\text{ Also assume that }P_R(\cdot)\text{ is set to (6.1.61) and }\mu\text{ is chosen such that }\mu\le\frac{D_f}{(n+4)\sqrt{2N}}.\text{ Then, under Assumptions 13 and 15, }\frac{1}{L}\mathbb{E}[\|\nabla f(x_R)\|^2]\le\bar{\mathscr{B}}_N:=\frac{12(n+4)LD_f^2}{N}+\frac{4\sigma\sqrt{n+4}}{\sqrt{N}}\left(\widetilde{D}+\frac{D_f^2}{\widetilde{D}}\right)

key_lemmas.name: martingale_second_moment_Lemma_6_1
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Assume that we are given a polish space with Borel probability measure }\mu\text{ and a sequence of }\mathcal{F}_0=\{\varnothing,\Omega\}\subseteq\mathcal{F}_1\subseteq\mathcal{F}_2\subseteq\cdots\text{ of }\sigma\text{-sub-algebras of the Borel }\sigma\text{-algebra of }\Omega.\text{ Let }\zeta_i\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ i=1,\ldots,\infty,\text{ be a martingale-difference sequence of Borel functions on }\Omega\text{ such that }\zeta_i\text{ is }\mathcal{F}_i\text{ measurable and }\mathbb{E}[\zeta_i\mid\mathcal{F}_{i-1}]=0,\text{ where }\mathbb{E}[\cdot\mid\mathcal{F}_i]\text{ denotes conditional expectation with respect to }\mathcal{F}_i\text{ and }\mathbb{E}\equiv\mathbb{E}[\cdot\mid\mathcal{F}_0].\text{ (a) If }\mathbb{E}[\|\zeta_i\|^2]\le\sigma_i^2\text{ for any }i\ge1,\text{ then }\mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\sum_{i=1}^N\zeta_i\right\|^2\right]\le\sum_{i=1}^N\sigma_i^2.\text{ As a consequence, }\operatorname{Prob}\left\{\left\|\sum_{i=1}^N\zeta_i\right\|^2\ge\lambda\sum_{i=1}^N\sigma_i^2\right\}\le\frac{1}{\lambda},\quad \forall N\ge1,\lambda\ge0.
key_lemmas.role: Controls the averaged post-optimization residuals in (6.1.89) and (6.1.90).
key_lemmas.citation: The paper cites Theorem 2.1 of [57] for Lemma 6.1.
